description: The line plot illustrates the performance of various dense retrieval methods in terms of MRR@10 (Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10) as a function of the number of queries used during inference, with the x-axis representing the number of queries used during inference in seconds (ranging from 0 to 8) and the y-axis showing the MRR@10 score (ranging from approximately 34.0 to 5.0). The plot compares six different methods: DPR w/o query (black solid line), DPR w/ gold (yellow dashed line), DPR w/ top-1 (green dash-dotted line), DPR w/ bottom-1 (purple dotted line), DPR w/ random (blue dashed line), and DPR w/ curriculum (red dash-dotted line). The DPR w/ curriculum method consistently achieves the highest MRR@10 scores across all query counts, starting at approximately 35.0 and increasing to around 5.0. The DPR w/ gold method shows a steady increase from about 34.5 to 35.5, while the DPR w/ top-1 method starts at a lower value and increases to around 35.5. The DPR w/ bottom-1 method remains relatively stable around 35.0, and the DPR w/ random method shows a slight increase from about 34.5 to 35.5. The DPR w/o query method remains constant at approximately 34.0 throughout the range. The legend clearly identifies each method with its corresponding line style and color, allowing for easy comparison of their performance trends.
